controller: WinMax Lathe (Hurco TM/TMX-class, DS Desktop sim) — on-site live-test target
description: WinMax LATHE 'courses' = named, ordered, VISION-FREE turning step-sequences, the lathe sibling of winmax-courses.json (mill). Same runner (scripts/winmax-course-run.mjs --courses <this>) + same PrismWinMaxUI UIA driver (attaches by process name, so it drives the lathe controller too — no driver copy needed, only this courses doc + a lathe FSM map). Turning differs from milling at the Tool Setup + Part Setup forms: a lathe tool carries NOSE RADIUS + ISO ORIENTATION (1-9) + X/Z geometry offsets (NOT mill diameter + cal-length), and turning safety is G96 CSS clamped by a G50 max-RPM. EVERY concrete field id + screen signature below is UNRESOLVED until a live WinMax-Lathe UIA probe captures it (the mill ids 301/303/310 will NOT match — the lathe Tool Geometry form is a different screen). This is the honest scaffold: course INTENT + lathe DOMAIN FACTS are encoded; the runner FAILS LOUD on any UNRESOLVED step in live mode (never fakes a pass). slot:echo. Turning cut-physics + safety (G96->G50 cap, parting L/D, chuck) route to WHISKEY; feed/speed to OSCAR.
siblingOf: winmax-courses.json (mill) — copy-modify lineage per operator directive 'copy the mill winmax setup and modify it for the lathe version'.

facts.unitsVerifyPerPart: JM convention is INCH (G20) but VERIFY per part from the source (NC G20/G21, CAM setup unit). A 25.4x mislabel is the #1 catastrophic error — every X/Z below is treated as the program's declared unit, NOT assumed.
facts.turningToolGeometry: A WinMax lathe Tool Setup entry carries: TOOL NUMBER, NOSE RADIUS (insert tip radius), ISO TOOL ORIENTATION (1-9, the tip quadrant for G41/G42 nose-radius comp), X GEOMETRY OFFSET (diameter), Z GEOMETRY OFFSET (face). This REPLACES the mill DIAMETER + CAL-LENGTH pair — the field ids are a DIFFERENT screen and must be probed live.
facts.cssClampSafety: Turning uses G96 constant-surface-speed; it MUST be clamped by a G50 max-RPM or a small-diameter feature commands a chuck-overspeed. The verify course confirms a G50 clamp is present (whiskey owns the physics; echo confirms the dialect emits it).
facts.partZeroTurning: Lathe part-zero: X is on the spindle centerline (diameter mode, X=0 at center), Z=0 at the finished face. The work-offset form fields differ from the mill XYZ form.
facts.fieldInputRecipeUnverified: ASSUME the mill recipe carries over (click <id> -> type-raw '<digits>' -> commit), but VERIFY on the lathe controller — the lathe forms may use different commit keys. Marked unverified until a live probe confirms.
facts.driverIsShared: PrismWinMaxUI.exe attaches by process name (--process 'WinMax'), so the SAME UIA driver drives the lathe controller. No winmax-lathe-bridge/ C# copy is required — the lathe-specific knowledge lives in THIS courses doc + a lathe FSM map (winmax-lathe-ui-map, to be probed).

fingerprint-lathe-screens.goal: DISCOVERY course: walk the lathe controller's menus and fingerprint each screen to build the lathe FSM map (winmax-lathe-ui-map). Run this FIRST against the live WinMax Lathe before any field course — it resolves the UNRESOLVED ids the other courses need. READ-ONLY (no field writes, no motion).
